Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
7 October 2026 .
Brent $ 101.87 + 3.71 % · Transits 4 (2026-10-04) · AI-assisted
01 Brent stood at $101.87, up 3.71% over 24 hours, as of 14:38 UTC; IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on 2026-10-04, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

Situation
Reuters reports an Iranian official has said 'illegal routes' in the strait will soon be blocked, a declaration that sits alongside the operational reality captured by the Financial Times: tanker captains are earning $100,000 a month in risk pay as freight rates soar 26-fold, indicating some transits continue. The closure picture is contested between those two positions, and this site's verdict on carrier posture remains a cautious closed. gCaptain and Al Jazeera report Houthi forces attacked Aden airport as fighting intensifies in Yemen, with Saudi forces downing a missile near Riyadh. IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on 2026-10-04, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. Brent stood at $101.87, up 3.71% over 24 hours, as of 14:38 UTC. Fifty-three events have been indexed in the last 24 hours. As of 14:50 UTC, 155 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, flat over 24 hours, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the elevated band, flat over 24 hours, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
